nodes.summary: Algebra studies structures defined by operations and the laws, morphisms, and symmetries that organize them.
nodes.title: Algebra

nodes.summary: Combinatorics studies finite and discrete configurations through counting, extremal structure, and constructive arguments.
nodes.title: Combinatorics

nodes.summary: Algebraic geometry studies spaces cut out by polynomial equations and translates between their geometric and algebraic invariants.
nodes.title: Algebraic Geometry

nodes.summary: Ring theory studies addition and multiplication through ideals, modules, localization, dimension, and homological structure.
nodes.title: Ring Theory

nodes.summary: Analysis studies limits, approximation, continuity, and infinite-dimensional spaces of functions and operators.
nodes.title: Analysis

nodes.summary: Measure theory provides the language of size and integration underlying probability and modern analysis.
nodes.title: Measure Theory

nodes.summary: Geometry studies shapes, spaces, transformations, curvature, and the invariants preserved by geometric equivalence.
nodes.title: Geometry

nodes.summary: Linear algebra studies vector spaces, linear maps, matrices, duality, dimension, and spectral structure.
nodes.title: Linear Algebra

nodes.summary: Number theory studies integers, primes, Diophantine equations, arithmetic functions, and their analytic and algebraic structure.
nodes.title: Number Theory

nodes.summary: Mathematical biology models populations, genomes, and biochemical networks, from coalescents and reaction dynamics to the algorithms that read biological sequences.
nodes.title: Mathematical Biology

nodes.summary: Computer science formalizes algorithms, programming-language structures, data abstractions, and correctness properties.
nodes.title: Computer Science

nodes.summary: Information theory quantifies information, uncertainty, compression, and transmission through entropy and coding.
nodes.title: Information Theory

nodes.summary: Probability studies random phenomena through distributions, expectation, independence, concentration, and stochastic processes.
nodes.title: Probability

nodes.summary: Graph theory studies vertices and edges through connectivity, coloring, minors, flows, and extremal structure.
nodes.title: Graph Theory

nodes.summary: Category theory organizes mathematical structures through morphisms, functors, universal properties, limits, and adjunctions.
nodes.title: Category Theory

nodes.summary: Dynamics studies systems evolving through iteration or time, including recurrence, stability, and long-term behavior.
nodes.title: Dynamical Systems

nodes.summary: Logic studies formal languages, proof, models, semantics, consistency, and the foundations of mathematical reasoning.
nodes.title: Logic

nodes.summary: Order theory studies comparison relations, lattices, intervals, monotonicity, and order-complete constructions.
nodes.title: Order Theory

nodes.summary: Field theory studies extensions of fields, algebraic elements, automorphisms, and Galois-theoretic structure.
nodes.title: Field Theory

nodes.summary: Game theory studies strategic and combinatorial interaction, equilibria, winning conditions, and optimal play.
nodes.title: Game Theory

nodes.summary: The mathematical study of what can be computed and at what cost: machine models, computability and undecidability, automata and formal languages, and computational complexity.
nodes.title: Theory of Computation

nodes.summary: Topology studies continuity, open sets, compactness, connectedness, and invariants preserved by homeomorphism.
nodes.title: Topology

nodes.summary: Statistical mechanics studies lattice models of interacting spins and bonds through Gibbs measures, partition functions, correlation inequalities, and phase transitions.
nodes.title: Statistical Mechanics

nodes.summary: Group theory studies symmetry through groups, actions, subgroups, quotients, and structural decompositions.
nodes.title: Group Theory

nodes.summary: Quantum information studies states, channels, measurement, entanglement, communication, and quantum computation.
nodes.title: Quantum Information

nodes.summary: Representation theory studies symmetry by realizing groups and algebras as transformations of linear spaces.
nodes.title: Representation Theory

nodes.summary: Set theory studies membership, cardinality, ordinals, infinity, and foundational constructions for mathematics.
nodes.title: Set Theory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
